newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil coffee council to discuss producer debts.
newsitem.headline: Brazil coffee council to discuss producer debts.

text.p: Brazil's coffee council, the CDPC, is to hold its second official session in Belo Horizonte, Minas Gerais state, on May 7, with one of the main themes the restructuring of producer debt, officials said.

CDPC president Industry and Commerce Minister Francisco Dornelles and 12 council members - six from the private sector and six government officials - will examine a report drawn up by Rio de Janeiro-based think-tank Fundacao Getulio Vargas (FGV).
In the report, total producer debt is estimated at around 581 million reais ($548 million), traders said.
Of this, the FGV is looking to tackle the problem of the 212 million reais which are non-securitised using resources from the Funcafe coffee fund.

The remaining loans are either securitised Funcafe loans (164.50 million reais), farm credits with Banco do Brasil (124.50 million reais) or loans from private banks and other sources (80 million reais).
The FGV report suggests the first repayment of 10 percent of the 212 million reais be made in November 1998 and then 15 percent each following year for a six-year period.

If frosts or any other climatic disaster hits the crop, the financial agent would have 60 days to find out the extent of the damage and could agree to delay payments for three years if there is severe damage, two years for middling damage and one year for light damage.

The report also allows for problems due to any sharp fall in coffee prices in that it allows farmers to repay in coffee, should the average price in the four months prior to the payment month fall below an agreed level.
This producers can do twice during the seven-year period.
Interest rates would be the long-term interest rate (TJLP) plus three percent, traders said.
For new credits, the report suggests some 200 million reais should be made available immediately to cover harvest costs. Repayment should be within 90 days at most at the TJLP plus three percent .
A further 150 million reais should be made available through July to September for stock financing. Loans would be for up to 120 days at the TJLP plus six percent.
A further 250 million reais should then released from September to prepare for the next harvest to be repayed in instalments by April 1998 at TJLP plus six percent.
The initial reaction from producers is positive, said Gilson Ximenes, president of the National Coffee Council which represents growers.

"It is very good...There are still things that need to be talked about such as the form and timetable for payments for the new loans but I have talked to people and they think the amount of money is sufficient," Ximenes said.
Exporters also cautiously welcomed the proposal although likewise said that the details of some aspects needed to be discussed in more depth.

"It is in line with reality. It is a very good beginning for a new coffee policy which doesn't exist but there is still a lot to be discussed," said Oswaldo Aranha, president of the Brazilian Coffee Exporters Federation (Febec).

Council members will informally discuss the proposal at a meeting in Belo Horizonte this afternoon but traders anticipate the council tomorrow approve the restructuring of the old loans plus the release of the 200 million for the harvest.
Credits for stock financing and for preparation for the 1998/99 harvest may need to be discussed further however.
The council is not expected to come to any decisions on what should be Brazil's position at the upcoming meeting of the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) in London.
The ACPC secretariat has asked members to submit ideas on whether and how the ACPC should continue a scheme to stabilise prices which at present is in the form of export controls.
The head of the primary commodities department at the Industry and Commerce Ministry Mauricio Assis insists however Brazil's position will only be defined in London.
"There will be no decision until London," he said.
((-Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151))
